target.title: fix(message): preserve stringified channelData payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where message actions that pass channel-specific `channelData` as a JSON string could lose that payload or fail to treat it as send content when the visible text is blank or removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message tool, outbound runner, and embedded subscribe rich-content tracker now parse `channelData` with the same structured JSON boundary used for sibling message payload fields. The shared structured-content helpers keep oversized legacy files from growing while preserving the same dispatch behavior. The message-tool path also rejects opaque `channelData` that contains protected internal runtime context before dispatch, and the runner now counts valid object-shaped `channelData` as real send content without adding config, schema, provider, or compatibility behavior.

Duplicate search found no open or closed overlapping PRs or open issues for `channelData JSON message action`, `stringified channelData`, `message-tool channelData idempotency`, or `parseJsonMessageParam channelData`; open self PRs had no same-root outbound/message parameter normalization overlap.

## User Impact

Channel-native cards, buttons, and other provider payload metadata can be preserved when passed as JSON strings, including internal source replies that intentionally carry channel-specific structured data without visible text. Protected runtime context remains filtered before those opaque payloads can be sent.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: stringified `channelData` is parsed before message-tool dispatch and outbound runner validation, channelData-only sends remain dispatchable after visible text is stripped, embedded rich-content detection still recognizes channelData-only payloads, and protected internal runtime context inside opaque channelData keys or values is removed before dispatch.
- Current head: `641c0c0fe8c4e302a92d0c1d25d236b62cbf9291`.
- Runtime transcript: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` directly executed `createMessageTool` with an injected dry-run outbound sink. Observed `safeChannelDataOnlyDispatched=true`, `safeVisibleMessageAfterSanitize=""`, `mixedChannelDataRemoved=true`, and `leakedBootMarker=false` for a stringified Slack-style `channelData` payload containing mixed prefix/suffix internal runtime context.
- Focused regression proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.send-validation.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts -t "channelData|rich-content|internal-runtime-context sanitization"` passed with 43 tests and 486 skipped.
- Targeted format: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src\agents\tools\message-tool.ts src\agents\tools\message-tool-content.ts src\infra\outbound\message-action-runner.ts src\agents\embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts src\infra\outbound\message-action-structured-content.ts` passed.
- LOC ratchet check: compared against CI base `f167089d6176dad5a32e361f541be9805ccc6cc3`; legacy files are no longer growing (`message-action-runner.ts` same at 1791 lines, `message-tool.ts` shrunk 1733 -> 1688, `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts` shrunk 1729 -> 1725), and the two new helper files are 86 and 54 lines.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD --codex-bin C:\Users\86158\.codex\codex-pixel-autoreview.cmd` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
